title: Jam the Bat
hook: Jam a bat that learns your rhythm.
sub: You're a tiger moth. Your ultrasonic clicks scramble the bat's sonar, but its AI learns your timing. Feed your click jitter from a metronome, a leaky seed packet, an emulator, or 156 qubits of IBM's ibm_fez, and see which one it can read.
you_control: Steer the moth (pointer, finger or arrow keys)
Click to jam: hold for a click train, tap for one click
Pick your noise-maker mid-flight: metronome, leaky seed packet, emulator box, or the ibm_fez / ibm_marrakesh chip
Run the bat tournament: 100-500 auto-rounds per source
qubits_note: comet-qrng-v1 on ibm_fez and on ibm_marrakesh: 148 register + 8 Bell-witness = 156 qubits each, reported by the job's provenance.circuit (n_rand 148, n_total 156); initial_layout covers physical qubits 0-155, the whole chip. Emulator runs at the 20-qubit emu cap (12+8 and 20+0).
honesty: Hardware banks are real comet-qrng-v1 outputs from all 156 qubits of ibm_fez (S = 2.543 +/- 0.015) and ibm_marrakesh (S = 2.728 +/- 0.015), entropy-accounted under a stated independence assumption but not certified (CHSH is a fidelity witness, not device-independent); the emulator bank is an uncertified classical baseline; the game, bat AI and tournament are classical, and the tournament shows hardware, emulator and secret-seed PRNG level (p = 0.93), with only the metronome and the leaked seed losing.
